title: Tribute to a multi-instrumentalist New Orleans friend
summary: Foster praises a friend who played trumpet, trombone, violin and piano and got him good jobs, with other pianists named.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: You let up my your friend, my man, that's the only man, and I was going to supper and drum about it one time. I don't know that one day. Tell them now.

And I don't want to get my own and there. You know the word Bo need a horse. That's what we called it. Always. Always. Huh? And we had some very good times together. We played with some of the best guys together. He got me on some of the best jobs that I could play on in New Orleans. And we had to do it. We played for the cream with the crocks on it. That's all I could say. We did.
Are you saying about the trombone and trumpet?
Did you ever see him play the trombone and trumpet together? Well, I liked him.

I had never seen him play his trombone and trumpet, but I know I liked his trumpet playing. And don't forget that violin. He played violin. And he played a whole lot of piano. All the piano he played, you want to hear. I've heard him do that.

Because spots he played on, Jelly Roll couldn't play that. And I'm not talking to him. I'm not talking to him. I'm talking to all the loud chords. Because he was back there on some good jobs when Tony Jackson and Georgia Thomas and them didn't have nothing to do. Black Pete and all those guys. U. L. Wilson. Albert Cowell. What's this other guy named? Or lived up on Broadway. Alfred Wilson. Alfred Wilson. Oh, yeah.
Yeah. As a king. Yeah. That's all.

They played a lot of jobs down there. Had a lot of pimples. Of course, they gave up music playing out much and devoting themselves. For 40 years. Teaching. They passed. Taught a lot of good. Well, the days.
